title: Reduced boundary of a smooth curve is smooth of dimension zero
statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field (every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable), let $C$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $j:U\to C$ be a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $i:Z\to C$ be the reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] closed complement [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $Z$ is a finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] $k$-scheme with $\dim Z\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (and $\dim Z=-\infty$ when $Z=\varnothing$), and its structure morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of pure relative dimension zero [def-weil-pure-dimension].

source.place: Step 2: the reduced scheme Z is a finite disjoint union of spectra of perfect fields, hence smooth of dimension zero

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $C=\bigcup_{a=1}^m\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ with each $A_a$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], the preimage in $Z$ of the $a$th member is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/I_a)$ for an ideal $I_a\subseteq A_a$. The images of any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $A_a$ generate $A_a/I_a$. These finitely many quotient spectra cover $Z$, proving that $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type by the same definition. Reducedness of $Z$ is part of the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), closed-immersion assertion, written out on the given finite affine cover

proof.text: Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C$ is contained in an irreducible component: apply [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] to its largest member. The chain remains a chain of closed irreducible subsets of that component. Each component has dimension one by [def-weil-pure-dimension], so the topological Krull dimension of $C$ is at most one (also when $C$ is empty). By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], this is the dimension hypothesis of [lem-pc-nowhere-dense-dim-zero]. The subset $|Z|=|C|\setminus U$ is closed with empty interior because $U$ is dense. Thus that lemma applies to the closed immersion $i$ and yields $\dim Z\le0$. Apply [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to $Z$ to express this as topological Krull dimension at most zero. If $Z$ is empty both dimensions in this comparison are $-\infty$, as explicitly included in the comparison lemma.

source.place: Tag 0AYY (lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor), proof sentence deducing dimension at most zero from nowhere density; dimension comparison: Properties Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian], the finite-type zero-dimensional scheme Z is locally Artinian and its underlying space is discrete and compact, hence finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine] to Z itself, obtaining Z = Spec A with A its ring of global sections. This includes the empty scheme and the zero ring. The ring A is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme], Artinian by local Artinianness and affineness, and of finite type over k by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The Artinian finite-type criterion Module.finite_of_isArtinianRing (Mathlib.RingTheory.Jacobson.Artinian) therefore makes A finite-dimensional over k. No singleton identifications or scheme coproducts are needed.

source.place: Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), finite-type zero-dimensional schemes are affine and finite over the base field; the Lean proof uses Artinian.lean and Module.finite_of_isArtinianRing.

proof.text: Identify the global sections R of Spec k with k through Scheme.ΓSpecIso; transport the field and perfect-field structures along this ring equivalence. The affine morphism f induces an R-algebra structure on A. Apply [lem-a1-finite-reduced-perfect-algebra-etale] to this finite reduced algebra over the perfect field R. The affine ring-homomorphism criterion HasRingHomProperty.iff_of_isAffine transports its etaleness to Etale f. Mathlib instances Etale -> SmoothOfRelativeDimension 0 and Etale -> Smooth give the two asserted smoothness conclusions (the definitions in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]). Together with the finite-type and dimension conclusions from the earlier steps, and the empty supremum formula for Scheme.dim in the empty case, this proves the conjunction.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field); compare Morphisms Tags 02GL and 02GK. Lean affine and smooth-relative-dimension-zero criteria: Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Etale.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06LH, with Algebra Tag 00U3. Shorter affine/global-sections route using the already proved Algebra.Etale.of_isReduced_of_perfectField, retaining the blueprint boundary geometry and the original dimension-drop argument.
